title: Motion (*.mtn) Open/Save
content: ### Objective Motion is a native file format (*mtn) of Marvelous Designer that saves Avatar movement information, and is used when recording Animation of Garments and Avatars. Marvelous Designer provides Motion files for its default male and female Avatars, but Animation Data or Motion capture Data from third-party 3D solutions can be imported as COLLADA files, then extracted as a Motion file (*mtn) through this menu. ### Location #### Open Motion Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Open ▶ Joint Motion #### Save Motion Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Save As ▶ Joint Motion ### Operation #### Open Motion 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Open ▶ Joint Motion → The Open File window appears. 2. Navigate to the desired *mtn file, then click Open. → The Load Motion Type window appears. 3. Select from the available settings: Joint Information | Joint Rotation & Translation | Applies the Avatar's Height, Pose, Motion Data (Joint rotation,) and Joint positions ---|---|--- Joint Rotation Only | Applies the Pose Motion Data (Joint rotation) only, while maintaining the Avatar's Size. Garment Position | Move Avatar & Garment to Start Position | Moves the Avatar and Garment to the location of the first frame (ver 2.5.0). Transition Animation | A transition Animation is an Animation that changes from a T-Pose to a motion's first Pose in stages, and is created when the Avatar's current Pose and Motion differs from that of the first frame Pose. → The motion (*mtn) file loads according to the settings. #### Save Motion 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Save As ▶ Joint Motion → The Save File window appears. 2. Type in file name and designate the path the file will be saved to. → The Motion (*mtn) file will be saved to the designated path. ※ Note: * Motion files can only be saved when imported as Avatars in COLLADA format with Motion Data, and the COLLADA files must be in Open COLLADA format. * To learn more about COLLADA format, please reference [3D File (COLLADA) Import](https://marvelousdesigner-hc.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/47358302910361). * The Transition Animation for default avatars of version10 is not compatible with the previous versions.
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide on how to open and save Objective Motion files (*mtn) in Marvelous Designer, facilitating the recording and management of Avatar movement data for garment animations.

title: ZIPPER: Create Zippers
content: ### Objective Create and use Zippers quickly and easily. ### Location Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Zipper ▶ Zipper 3D Toolbar ▶ Zipper ### Operation 1. Navigate to the location listed below: 3D Toolbar ▶ Zipper 2. Click on the 3D garment or 2D Patterns (ver MD10) where the Zipper should be attached, then move the cursor. → Based on the direction the cursor is moved, the segment where the Zipper appears is highlighted in light blue. 3. Double click on the desired endpoint for the Zipper. → One side of the Zipper is created. 4. Click on the Pattern outline where the other side of the Zipper is attached, then move the cursor. → Based on the direction the cursor is moved, a blue point appears indicating the same length as the first half of the Zipper which was created in step 3. 5. Double click on the blue point. → The Zipper is now complete, along with a Puller, Slider, and Stopper (ver MD10). 6. Activate the Simulation. → The Zipper simulates in a closed/fully zipped state. → To unzip the Zipper, click on the Zipper in the 3D Window WITHOUT the Gizmo active, and drag to move the Zipper (referenced in dark grey) along the length of the Zipper Tape. ※ Note: #### Cancel Actions during Zipper Creation * Cancel All Actions While using the Zipper tool, press 'Esc' or 'Ctlr +Z' on the keyboard, and all actions will be undone. * Cancel Last Action While using the Zipper tool, press the 'Delete' or 'Backspace' Key on the keyboard and the last action will be undone.
content_description: This web page provides a quick and easy guide to creating and simulating zippers in 3D garment design using the Zipper tool in the 3D Toolbar.

title: Create 2D Measurements
content: ### Internal Shape ### Objective View the position of Internal Shapes from the Pattern outline with 2D measurements (ver2.5.0). ### Location Property Editor ▶ 2D Measurements ▶ To Outline/To Center ### Operation 1. 2D Toolbar ▶ Transform Pattern Tool ▶ Select the Internal Shape/Dart. 2. Follow the indicated guideline below: Property Editor ▶ 2D Measurements ▶ To Outline/To Center 3. Select the desired 2D Measurements to display. To Outline View | the 2D Measurements from the left, right, top, and bottom of the Internal Shape to the Pattern outline. ---|--- To Center View | the 2D Measurements from the center of the Internal Shape to the left, right, top, and bottom of the Pattern outline. →2D Measurements appear based on the selected items. ### Internal Line ### Objective View the position of Internal Lines or segments of Internal Shapes from the Pattern outline with 2D Measurements (ver2.5.0). ### Location Property Editor ▶ 2D Measurements ▶ To Center ### Operation 1. 2D Toolbar ▶ Transform Pattern Tool ▶ Select the Internal Shape/Dart. 2. Follow the indicated guideline below: Property Editor ▶ 2D Measurements ▶ To Outline/To Center 3. Select the desired 2D Measurements to display. → 2D Measurements appear based on the selected items. ### Internal Point ### Objective View the position of internal points or internal curve points from the Pattern outline with 2D Measurements (ver2.5.0). ### Location Property Editor ▶ 2D Measurements ▶ To Center ### Operation 1. 2D Toolbar ▶ Transform Pattern Tool ▶ Select the Internal Shape/Dart. 2. Follow the indicated guideline below: Property Editor ▶ 2D Measurements ▶ To Outline/To Center 3. Select the desired 2D Measurements to display. → 2D Measurements appear based on the selected items.
content_description: This web page provides detailed instructions for viewing and measuring the positions of internal shapes, lines, and points relative to the pattern outline using 2D measurements in version 2.5.0.

Set Increments for Arrow Keys Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Preferences ▶ 2D Pattern Window Properties (F12) ▶ Property Editor ▶ Arrow Key Movement Right Click Pop-Up Menu (On 2D Window) ▶ 2D Pattern Window Properties (F12)▶ Property Editor ▶ Arrow Key Movement 2\. title: Select/Move Point/Segment
content: ### ### ### Objective Modify Patterns and Internal Shapes by moving points and segments. ### Location Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ Edit Pattern 2D Toolbar ▶ Edit Pattern ### Operation #### Select 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ Edit Pattern 2D Toolbar ▶ Edit Pattern 2. Click a point or segment of a Pattern or Internal Shape. → The point or segment is selected. → When there are multiple points or segments, a pop-up menu appears allowing you to select the desired one (ver3.0.0.) 3. To select multiple points and segments, hold down the Shift key on the keyboard when clicking them. → All clicked points and segments are selected. 4. Or, click and drag on the 2D window to encompass points and segments to be selected with the marquee box. → All points and segments inside the marquee box are selected. → The Transform pattern tool's selection box can now select patterns no matter the area it covers; by holding CTRL and clicking and dragging your mouse. (ver. 2024.0) #### Move 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ Edit Pattern 2D Toolbar ▶ TEdit Pattern 2. Click and drag the Pattern or use the arrow keys. 3. Hold down the Shift key or Ctrl key (Mac: command) while moving the point or segment. → The point or segment can be moved in precise vertical, horizontal, or diagonal lines, or in its slope. 4. Or, right click or hit F1 key (Mac: Ctrl) while moving the point or segment to type in distance moved. Option | Description ---|--- Distance Moved | Type in the how much a segment or a point is moved. X-Axis (ver4.2.0) | Type in how much a point is moved on x-axis. This option does not appear for segments. Y-Axis (ver4.2.0) | Type in how much a point is moved on Y-axis. This option does not appear for segments. ※ Note: If it is cumbersome to select Patterns using the Edit Pattern tool, use the Transform Pattern tool.
content_description: This webpage provides instructions for modifying patterns and internal shapes in a 2D environment by selecting and moving points and segments using various tools and keyboard shortcuts.

title: 3D Garment Information (ver4.1.0 and Above)
content: ### Objective Write and check important Garment information. ### Location Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Information ▶ Garment ### Operation #### Enter Default Garment Information 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Information ▶ Garment → The Garment Information window appears. 2. Click the Edit icon on the right top corner of the window. → The Garment Information window changed to the edit mode. 3. Type in necessary information next to each category and click OK. → Typed in information is saved. #### Add Category 1. Refer to Enter Default Garment Information manual to active the edit mode. 2. Click the Add icon. → A category is added. Click the drop-down menu and select desired category. → There are eight categories to choose from: Code, Name, Description, Price, Fabric, Size, Colorway, Category, and Memo. 3. Type in necessary information for each category and click OK. → Typed in information is saved. #### Reorder Category 1. Refer to Enter Default Garment Information manual to active the edit mode. 2. Click and drag the category to the desired position. → The category is moved to where the mouse is released. 3. When categories are re-ordered completely, click OK. → Revised category order is saved. #### Delete Category 1. Refer to Enter Default Garment Information manual to active the edit mode. 2. Click the Delete icon next to each category. → The selected category is deleted. 3. When the editing is completed, click OK. → The deleted category no longer appears in the Garment Information window. ※ Note: * Toggle on Display When Garment File Loads option to open the Garment Information window every time the file opens. * Open or save Garment information such as categories, order, and contents by using the Open and Save buttons on the right top corner of the edit mode. * Use the Default File setting to designate default Garment Information file.
content_description: This web page serves as a comprehensive guide for users to enter, edit, organize, and manage essential garment information efficiently.

title: Wind Controller Setting
content: ### Objective Adjust and apply wind effect to create fluttering effect on garment in the 3D window. ### Location Main Menu ▶ Display ▶ Show Wind Controller ### Operation #### Activate Wind Effect 1\. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Display ▶ Environment ▶ Show Wind Controller → Cone-shaped Wind Controller appears in the 3D window. ![11.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438677359257) 2\. Click the Wind Controller. → Wind Controller properties appear in the Property Editor. 3\. Wind ▶ Toggle on (Check Box) at Activate. → It is now being activated (Toggled On) and becomes in blue color. ![22.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438687951001) 4\. Click Simulation. → The Wind Effect is now being activated in the 3D window. #### Wind Direction Setting 1\. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Display ▶ Show Wind Controller → Cone-shaped Wind Controller appears in the 3D window. ![33.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438688142617) 2\. Click the Wind Controller. → Wind Controller Gizmo activates. 3\. Use the Gizmo to set direction and location of the wind. 4\. Click Simulation. → The Wind Effect is now being activated as adjusted in the 3D window. #### Wind Properties Setting 1\. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Display ▶ Show Wind Controller → Cone-shaped Wind Controller appears in the 3D window. 2\. Click the Wind Controller. → Wind Controller properties appear in the Property Editor. 3\. Adjust the default values at Property Editor according to the needs. Name | Changes name of the wind according to the user preference. ---|--- Wind | Activate | Sets the activation status of the wind. Type | Sets the type of the wind. Spherical: The wind blows in spherical shape, in every direction starting from the Wind Controller. ![44.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438688303641) Planar: The wind blows only from the designated direction, regardless of the Wind Controller's location. ![55.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438688411929) Strength | Sets the intensity of the wind. The higher the value, the stronger the wind. Decay [0~100] | Sets the range of the wind. The wind draws an arc and blows weaker according to the set value of wind intensity. If the value is "0", it blows in a straight line endlessly. Frequency (sec) | Sets the cycle of the wind. The wind repeatably blows weaker and stronger in interval of set value of seconds. If the value is "0", it blows regularly. Turbulence [0~100] | Sets the turbulence of wind intensity. The higher the value, the more irregular the wind intensity.
content_description: This webpage provides a comprehensive guide on how to activate and customize the wind effect for a fluttering garment simulation in a 3D environment.

Object Browser ▶ Topstitch Tab ▶ Property Editor ▶ Topstitch Texture ▶ Normal Map → The intensity value range of -10 to 10 can be applied automatically as entered. → The higher the value, the bumpier expression of top-stitches, the less the value, the less bumpier expression of top-stitches. #### Apply Topstitch Normal Map Image 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser ▶ Topstitch Tab ▶ Property Editor ▶ Topstitch Texture ▶ Normal Map 2. Click on the Search button. 3. Select and load desired texture image file. → The selected image is now being applied. ※ Note: Applying method for Topstitch Normal Map is the same as Fabric Texture Normal Map.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for applying normal maps to topstitches to enhance their realism in visualizations.

title: Use Layer (Drape Additional Garment)
content: ### Objective This function allows easier simulation when setting which layer to get in/outward among overlapped multiple layers. By using this function, taking out inaccurately inwardly simulated patterns such as pockets and buttons, gets easier. In addition, adding additional outerwear on top of garments such as dress and shirts. The default layer value of zero ('0') means the layer function is being off. In that state, the arrangement order of the patterns gets decided. ### Location Click Pattern ▶ Property Editor ▶ Simulation Properties ▶ Layer ### Operation 1. Select a pattern in the 3D window to set a layer with Select/Move tool. ※ Note: Select patterns in the 2D window, in case of having difficulties when choosing in the 3D window. 2. Follow the guide below: Click Pattern ▶ Property Editor ▶ Simulation Properties ▶ Layer 3. Apply the value by clicking Simulate button. ※Note: * When the layer value is being set, the patterns become highlighted in blue outline. Once the draping in desired order is completed, set the value back to zero ('0') for more stable simulation. (There is no change in draping even after modifying the value back to zero('0')). If the layer value is zero('0'), but the menu appears in red when all patterns are being selected, it is because there is a variety of values being mixed. Therefore revert the layer value to zero('0') once again. * Right-click to open the 3D Background Options Menu ▶ Show/Hide Color [(Show/Hide 3D Color Ver. 2024.1)](https://marvelousdesigner-hc.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/47358311619225)[ ](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/en-us/articles/32523191112473/preview/eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9.eyJpZCI6MzI1MjMxOTExMTI0NzMsImV4cCI6MTcxNTk3NDk0Mn0.vTz8AEFpwglRHaNeFb09thKYnyuNna7SAvTfH7sSS8U)to hide the layered patterns outline highlight color in the 3D window. ## Show layer Depth (Ver. 2024.1) ### Objective Toggle view option in the 2D window to display the layer number and color code to help visualize layers. ### ### Location 2D Window ▶ ![](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438439322905)2D Information ▶ ![](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438501035801)Show Pattern Layer ### Operation 1. Follow the guideline for Apply Layer Value to number different pattern layers: 2. Select and enter desired Layer number on selected pattern or multiple patterns. →Layer value is assigned 3. Set different layer values for other patterns. 4. Click the ![](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438501035801)Show Pattern Layer option under ![](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438439322905)2D information icon to activate. → Number of layer will be indicated and patterns with the same layer will be the same color 5. Click the ![](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438501035801)Show Pattern Layer option again to inactivate it. ※ Note: * The color values for each layer are as follows. * Layer 0 has one unique color: Light Gray * Layers 1 to 23 each have different color values. This repeats from 24 onwards. * ![image-20240415-003712.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438439968665) * Negative Layers are applied in the reverse order of positive numbers. * Layer depth display will automatically turn off when switching to another [2D Pattern Rendering Style](https://marvelousdesigner-hc.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/47358205499033). ### End Result Quickly visualizing and controlling layers is now convenient and intuitive
content_description: This web page provides a guide for simulating and managing overlapping layers in garment design, enabling users to easily adjust layer settings for improved pattern accuracy and visualization.

content: ### Objective Adjust speed of Animation frames (ver2.5.0). ### Location Animation Mode ▶ Animation Editor ▶ Scene Time Warp ### Operation 1\. Follow the indicated guideline below: Animation Mode ▶ Animation Editor ▶ Scene Time Warp 2\. Enter desired value and press Enter on the keyboard. → Frame rate for all Garment/Avatar Animation in the Animation Editor is now being adjusted according to the entered value.
content_description: This web page provides instructions for adjusting the animation frame speed in version 2.5.0 of the Animation Editor.

title: Button Property Setting
content: ### Objective Adjust button properties in the Property Editor. ### Location Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Button ▶ Select/Move Button 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move Button ### Explanation Selecting a button with Select/Move or Select/Move Button tool displays its properties in the Property Editor. Button Property | Description ---|--- Angle | Enter desired value for rotation angle of buttons. Thread Length (cm) | Enter desired value for thread length in centimeter (cm) from the range of 0.00~1.00. Style | Select a button style. Collision | Set ON/OFF for collision option. → Set it OFF in order to fix its location to avoid the collision between the buttons and the Patterns. 2D Measurements | View the position of buttons in 2D Pattern with its size measurement. Set check-boxes On for Left/Right/Up/Down as desired. → The 2D size measurements appear accordingly. Polygon Optimization | Count | Set the number of polygons. ---|---|--- Plane | This is applied in the form of a texture when the Plane is activated. Count cannot be set on Plane activation.
content_description: This web page provides guidance on adjusting button properties using the Property Editor, including rotation angle, thread length, style selection, collision settings, and 2D measurements.

title: Mirror Paste
content: ### Objective Mirror Paste copied Pattern/Internal Shape. ### Location Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on Pattern/Internal Shape) ▶ Mirror Paste (Ctrl + R) ### Operation 1. Navigate to 2D toolbar and select Transform Pattern Tool or Edit Pattern Tool. Then, copy the desired Pattern or Internal Shape. 2. Follow the indicated guideline below: Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on Pattern/Internal Shape) ▶ Mirror Paste (Ctrl + R) → The clone of copied Pattern/Internal Shape follows along the mouse cursor. 3. Click on the 2D window or on the Pattern to place the Pattern or the Internal Shape. ※ Note: * Hold down the Shift key on the keyboard to move the duplicated Pattern on a straight line or on a diagonal line. * Select the desired Pattern and hit Ctrl + C (Copy) / Ctrl +V(Paste), Ctrl + R(Mirror Paste) on the keyboard to copy and paste Patterns to a separate CLO window (ver3.0.0).
content_description: This web page provides a concise guide on using the Mirror Paste function in pattern design software to efficiently duplicate and manipulate patterns and internal shapes.

title: TOPSTITCH STYLE PROPERTIES: Exaggerate Topstitch
content: ### Objective Express the caved line when topstitches are stitched on the real garment. ### Location Object Browser ▶ Topstitch Tab ▶ Topstitch (Click Topstitch Style) ▶ Property Editor ▶ 3D ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guieline: Object Browser ▶ Topstitch Tab ▶ Topstitch (Click Topstitch Style) ▶ Property Editor ▶ 3D 2. Toggle on the 3D option. → 3D shadow is added under the Topstitch to express the caved line. 3. Use below options to adjust the caved line's Intensity or Thickness. Option | Description ---|--- Normal Map | Select the Normal Map. Intensity (%) | Adjust the caved line's intensity. Thickness | Adjust the caved line's thickness.
content_description: This webpage provides a step-by-step guide for utilizing the Topstitch feature in the Object Browser to effectively express caved lines on garments through 3D shadow adjustments.

title: Skive
content: ### Objective Add skiving effect on desired parts of a Pattern or all Patterns (ver2.3.0). ### Location Property Editor (Internal Shapes/Pattern Only) ▶ Bond/Skive ▶ Skive ### Operation 1. Select a pattern or an internal shape to express skiving with Edit Pattern or Transform Pattern tools. → Its properties appear in Property Editor. 2. Follow the indicated guideline below: Property Editor (Internal Shapes/Pattern Only) ▶ Bond/Skive ▶ Skive → The select Pattern/Internal Shape is now being displayed in a semi-transparent grey color. → A scrollbar appears, displaying the physical property of the pattern from the value range of zero ('0') to one hundred ('100') in Percentage (%). 3. Move the scrollbar to adjust as desired. 4. Activate the Simulate. → The area of the internal shape is now being displayed softer as if it has been shaved down.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for applying a skiving effect to patterns and internal shapes using the Property Editor in version 2.3.0.

title: Modify Piping Status
content: ### Objective Modify Piping status. ### Location 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move or Edit Piping ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move or Edit Piping 2. Right click on a desired piping to edit. → Piping pop-up menu appears. Pop-up Menu | Definition ---|--- Delete | Delete the selected Piping. Refresh All Piping | Re-drape all Piping. Deactivate/Activate | Deactivate/Activate selected Piping. Freeze/Unfreeze | Freeze/Unfreeze selected Piping. Quadranglate | Change Piping mesh to quads. Triangulate | Change Piping mesh to triangles. Hide | Hide selected Piping. Show All Piping | Show all Piping.
content_description: This webpage provides a comprehensive guide for modifying the status of piping within a 3D environment using the toolbar options and pop-up menu functionalities.

title: Set Shortcuts (Above ver4.2.0)
content: ### Objective Change the default settings of the software menu according to user preference in User Settings. Upon restarting, the user settings of the software becomes the default settings. Shortcut keys, menus, graphic options, view controls, default files, font settings and other miscellaneous properties can be set in User Settings. ### Location Main Menu ▶ Settings ▶ User Settings ▶ Shortcuts Main Menu ▶ Settings/Preferences ▶ Preferences ▶ Shortcuts (ver 11) ### Operation 1. Navigate to the menu as below: Main Menu ▶ Settings ▶ User Settings ▶ Shortcut Search (ver MD10) | Can search by menu name and shortcut key. When you select a search result, the location of the corresponding menu is displayed in the lower function window. ---|--- Function | Can search shortcuts based on the location of the menu. Click the menu for which you want to set a shortcut and press the desired key on the keyboard. Reset: Returns the hotkey to the program default settings. Delete: Deletes the set shortcut. ※Note: Click the reset button at the bottom of the dialog to return to the default setting.
content_description: Customize your software experience by adjusting default settings and shortcut keys in User Settings, ensuring your preferences are saved upon restart.

title: Desaturation
content: ### Objective Use this function to maintain the texture of texture images or patterns while changing colors. ### Location Object Browser ▶ Fabric ▶Property Editor ▶ Material ▶ Texture ▶ Desaturation ### Operation #### Shadow Intensity 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser ▶ Fabric ▶Property Editor ▶ Material ▶ Texture ▶ Desaturation 2. Enter the Shadow Intensity value directly or move the scrollbar to adjust. → The Shadow Intensity is now being adjusted and applied. #### Shadow Brightness 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser ▶ Fabric ▶Property Editor ▶ Material ▶ Texture ▶ Desaturation 2. Enter the Shadow Brightness value directly or move the scrollbar to adjust. → The Shadow Brightness is now being adjusted and applied.
content_description: This web page provides guidance on maintaining the texture of images while adjusting color properties, specifically focusing on Shadow Intensity and Shadow Brightness settings.

title: Offset Pattern Outline
content: ### Objective Extend or retract (ver MD10) the Pattern outline while maintaining its original shape. ### Location Right Click Pop-Up Menu ▶ Offset Pattern Outline ### Operation 1. With the Transform Pattern tool or the Edit Pattern tool, select the entire or partial Pattern outline. 2. Follow the indicated guideline below: Right Click Pop-Up Menu ▶ Offset Pattern Outline → The Offset Pattern Outline Window appears. 3. Adjust following options as needed. **Option** | **Description** ---|--- Direction | Extend | Extend Pattern Outlines. Retract | Retract Pattern Outlines. (ver MD10) ※Note: Only Distance can be modified when Retract is selected. Distance | Set how much in distance the Pattern outline is extended. Number of Offsets | Set the number of offsets to be created. Total Distance | Total Distance = Distance x Number of Offsets Create Internal Line | Create Internal Lines at where the original Pattern outlines existed. Side Segment Type | Perpendicular | Extends the Pattern outline perpendicular to the selected Pattern outline. Extend Side Segments | Extends the Pattern outline while matching the angles of the segments on either side. Mirror | Extends the Pattern outline based on the corner angle created with the selected Pattern outline and its adjacent one. Default Corner | Extends the Pattern outline all around the selected segment or Pattern. Right Angled Corner | Extends the Pattern outline all around the selected segment or Pattern and converting corners to right angles. Unfilled Corner | Extends the Pattern outline all around the selected segment or pattern, except for corners. 4. Click OK. → The Pattern outlines are offset according to the settings. → Curve points are optimized automatically. (ver MD10)
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for users to extend or retract pattern outlines while preserving their original shape using the Offset Pattern Outline feature.

title: Edit 3D Garment Measure
content: ### Objective Edit 3D Garment Measure. ### Location Main Menu ▶ 3D Garment ▶ Measurement ▶ Edit Garment Measure 3D Toolbar ▶ Edit Garment Measure ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 3D Garment ▶ Measurement ▶ Edit Garment Measure 3D Toolbar ▶ Edit Garment Measure 2. Click on a 3D Garment Measure to edit. → The selected 3D Garment Measure is now being highlighted. → Its properties are now being appeared in the Property Editor. 3. Modify the properties of 3D Garment Measure. Linear Garment Measure | Circumference Garment Measure ---|--- Name | Rename the Linear Garment Measure. | Name | Rename the Circumference Garment Measure. Length | Confirm the length of the Linear Garment Measure. | Surface Length | Confirm the length of the Circumference Garment Measure. Square Width | Modify the width of the square that appears at the end of the Linear Garment Measure. | Circle Diameter | Modify the circle diameter that appears with the Circumference Garment Measure.
content_description: This web page provides instructions for editing 3D garment measurements, allowing users to modify properties such as names, lengths, and dimensions through an intuitive interface.
